current.text: Toronto added Kawhi Leonard in a trade that sent out Brandon Ingram. Leonard is the better player and uses more possessions.
He is a projected starter with Quickley, Barrett, Leonard and Poeltl. He is also in the expected closing five, a small and switchable group.
Most experts doubt he takes a big step forward next to Leonard. They see him as about a top 17 to 18 player in categories and call picks 9 to 14 too high.
In an auction mock he went for 35 USD, which the expert called about right. An ESPN ADP of 31 is too late for him.
He is a round two option next to Giannis Antetokounmpo in a punt FT% build.
Toronto has 15 back-to-backs, three of them in the fantasy playoffs.
Toronto is projected to win about 52 games and could be a top four team in the East. The roster is thin after the top seven.

durable.text: He is one of the best help rim protectors in the league and anchors Toronto's defense.
His shooting is a question mark.
He is a multi-category forward. His assists, steals and blocks are well above the pool, and his assists are rare for a frontcourt player.
Turnovers are his weak category, high for his position.

note: Yahoo (42 USD value, 47 average cost) and ESPN (48 value, 43 cost) price him well above the 31 USD he cost in our league last season, and the experts think ranks 13 to 15 are a bit too high with Kawhi Leonard taking possessions. A fair price for us is around 35 to 40 USD. His assists from the frontcourt, steals and blocks fit most builds, including punt TO and punt FT% next to Giannis. Early in the season, check whether his usage and assists hold up next to Leonard, and plan for three Toronto back-to-backs in the playoff weeks.
